literal: The absence of rain drops to the world of what nature, like that indeed is the king's absence of grace to the living beings.
translation: Just as the absence of rain brings ruin to the world, so does the absence of a king's grace bring misery to his subjects.
modern: மழைத்துளி இல்லாதிருப்பது உலகத்திற்கு எவ்வளவு துன்பமோ, அதுபோலவே அரசனுடைய அருள் இல்லாதிருப்பது அவனுடைய நாட்டில் வாழும் உயிர்களுக்குத் துன்பமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares the vital necessity of a ruler's grace to the necessity of rain for the world. The word 'துளி' refers to rain drops, representing the life-giving water that sustains all earthly existence. 'அளி' means grace, compassion, or benevolence, which is the essential quality a ruler must possess to protect their subjects. Just as the 'இன்மை' (absence) of rain causes the physical world to wither and perish, the 'இன்மை' (absence) of a king's compassion causes the 'வாழும் உயிர்க்கு' (living beings) under his rule to suffer and decline.
